events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
NS-0 routes this case: cancelled_by = driver (F3) and the driver asserted rider no-show (F12), so the fee stands or falls on NS-1's three conditions. The platform-confirmed arrival is a driver tap, not an auto-detection: "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 (F5), with the trace confirming NS-1 (i) ✓ and the GPS covering the wait with no hole.

NS-1 (ii) fails on the system record. At the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver 600 m from the pickup, and his closest approach in the whole trip was 599 m at 12:06:55 — he never came within 200 m (F5, F1, F2). driver_arrived_at is null, i.e. the platform never logged him at the pickup point (F4). System records (gps/timeline) override the driver's later written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" (F12). The driver's own advocate concedes this (D2, rebuttal to C2).

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while GPS placed him 600 m from the pickup point, so NS-1 (ii) fails: he was not at the pick-up location according to GPS data when he claimed arrival.

The driver never came within 200 m of the pickup at any time — his closest approach was 599 m at 12:06:55 — and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1 (i)/(ii) are not satisfied.

The driver's stationary period of 3 min 30 s (12:05:55–12:09:25) was spent 600 m from the pickup point, and he spent 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap, so the "continuous wait at the pickup point" required by NS-1 (iii) never occurred.
Because none of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is met, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged on the record must be fully refunded to the rider under NS-2.

The rider's messages confirm she was at the pickup point and could not find the car ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" at 12:07), while the driver's only reply was that he would cancel; the driver's later written statement that he waited at the pickup point is a bare claim contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which win.

The driver pressing "I'm Here" while GPS showed him 600 m away is an abuse of the arrival button, which supports the additional action flag_account under NS-2; his profile shows 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days, an additional (but not sole) ground for account review.

The traffic record shows no incident near the route and only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Jalan Besar with fair weather, so nothing excuses the driver's position or supports any claimed impossibility of reaching the pickup point.

weaknesses: The chat record is complete and the driver did tap "I'm Here" and did wait over 3 minutes in absolute time (F5, F10, F11), so the driver will argue he complied with the substance of the waiting rule; the rider's case depends entirely on the 600 m GPS distance defeating NS-1 (ii) and (iii).

The 200 m arrival radius is a data-layer parameter, not a published Ryde figure (G2); the driver may argue the pickup point's practical approach spans more than 200 m, though the record's closest approach of 599 m (F1) is far outside any plausible radius.

The rider's own account is only a chat message (F9); there is no independent rider-side location record in the fact table confirming she was at the pickup point, so the driver may contest her presence, though F4 shows the platform never logged him as arriving.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows my client's closest approach to the pickup point was 599 m at 12:06:55, and he stopped 600 m away from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 — so he was stationary and waiting, not refusing the trip or abandoning the job.

My client did tap "I'm Here" at 12:06:15, but the GPS at that moment placed him 600 m from the pickup point and he stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds afterwards; NS-1 (ii) therefore fails on the system record, and the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand — it must be refunded in full.

The platform never recorded arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), which confirms there is no system basis for the no-show fee and the correct outcome is refund_full for the rider, not a finding against the driver's conduct as a trip refusal.

The rider was contemporaneously at the pickup point and asked where the car was (chat #2 at 12:07: “I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?”), while my client's message asserted he was already there — the messages and the GPS conflict, and NS-1 requires the GPS position at the tap to control, so the fee fails.

The chat record is complete — 3 messages, all timestamped — so this is not an evidence-gap case requiring escalation; the disposition on NS-1 is determinable and should be refund_full of $6.61 (F6 fare fact).

My client cancelled with a stated reason of rider no-show rather than cancelling without any reason, so the least adverse characterization available is NS-3-style misjudgement of the pickup position; his 6.3-year, 4.67-rated account with 464 trips in 90 days should not be treated as fare abuse on this single mismatch.

There is no aggravating safety element: no incidents were recorded near the route, weather was fair, and the messages contain no threat, intimidation or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not warranted.

weaknesses: The core fact is against us: F1 and F5 show my client tapped "I'm Here" while 600 m from the pickup point and never entered the 200 m radius (0 s within 200 m), which squarely triggers NS-2 and, on NS-2's own terms, also invites a flag_account against the driver for misuse of the arrival button — I cannot ask the judge to treat the tap as compliant.

My client's written statement (F12) asserts he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" and the rider "never showed up", but F2 and F1 show a stationary position 600 m away from the pickup, and under the system-record-wins rule (and RD-5/G11 on unsupported statements) the statement is contradicted by GPS and cannot be relied on.

The rider's chat message (F9) is the rider's own contemporaneous message placing her at the pickup point, and it lines up with the GPS; the judge may additionally note that drivers with route/no-show history face account review under NS-2's flag for GPS-inconsistent arrival taps.

points.response: Not contested — F2 confirms the driver was stationary 12:05:55–12:09:25, but that only proves he was waiting somewhere; F2 places that stationary position 600 m from the pickup, so NS-1 (iii) still fails because the required wait at the pickup point never happened.
Conceded on the outcome: F5 shows the tap at 600 m and F1 shows he never came within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails and NS-2 requires full refund of the $6.61 — our brief is consistent with this.

Agreed on the refund, but the refund follows from NS-1 (ii) failing, not from the driver's conduct being excused: NS-2 imposes flag_account when the arrival tap is inconsistent with GPS, and F5 shows exactly that 600 m inconsistency.

Correct that the GPS at the tap controls and the fee fails; note also that the driver's chat message (F8 "I'm here already") was contradicted by the rider's contemporaneous F9 and by F1, which is what makes the tap an abuse of the arrival button rather than a mere misjudgement.

We agree the chat record is complete (F11) and no G12 escalation is needed; the record supports refund_full, and we ask additionally for the flag_account that NS-2 attaches to a GPS-inconsistent arrival tap.

NS-3 does not apply: that clause governs a driver who cancels without a valid reason, while here the driver asserted no-show and actually tapped "I'm Here" 600 m away (F5, F12), which is the NS-2 scenario — and NS-2 itself attaches flag_account, which a long clean account (F17) does not remove.

Not contested: there is no threat or dangerous-driving element (F8, F10), no incidents near the route (F14) and fair weather (F15), so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is sought — the case is decided on NS-1/NS-2 alone.

Conceded on the merits: F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 12:06:15 with the driver 600 m from the pickup, and F1 confirms he never came within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails and the $6.61 must be refunded under NS-2 — this is also exactly what my own brief (D2, D3) asked for.

I do not contest the failure of NS-1 (i)/(ii): F4 (driver_arrived_at null) and F1 (closest approach 599 m) are system records and control over my client's statement in F12, so no-show cannot be established.

The 3 min 30 s stationary period in F2 did occur, but it was spent 600 m from the pickup with 0 s inside 200 m (F5), so NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied — I accept the refund; the only thing I ask the judge not to do is read that same fact as an intent to defraud.
No dispute: since none of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is met, the $6.61 recorded in F3 and charged per F6 must be fully refunded under NS-2, which is the same refund_full outcome I requested in D5.

I accept that F12 loses to F1/F4, but F9 being a chat message is not itself proof the rider stood at the pickup point, and F9 does not show her waiting there — the record simply shows the driver was 600 m away (F1), which is enough for the refund without adding findings beyond the evidence.

The flag_account rider-side asks for under NS-2 is a sanction my client cannot resist on the tap alone (F5), but NS-2's flag is directed at GPS-inconsistent arrival taps, whereas F2 shows he did remain stationary 3 min 30 s before cancelling rather than cancelling instantly, and F17's single upheld no-show in 90 days is a profile fact that cannot decide the case.

This point is immaterial to the outcome: F13, F14 and F15 show no incident, only band 3 on Jalan Besar and fair weather, and I have never pleaded a justified reroute, so RD-4 is not in issue in this no-show case.
